claims.text: The reported HfNbTiVAl10 state contains a hierarchical heterostructure.
The hierarchical heterostructure contains multilevel chemical fluctuations.
The hierarchical-heterostructured state can be produced by arc melting.
Small composition changes alter the hierarchical heterostructure.
The hierarchical heterostructure mediates the mechanical response of HfNbTiVAl10.
VEC and composition dictate phase formation in this alloy system.
VEC and composition dictate structural organization in this alloy system.
A surrogate trained on a limited set of high-fidelity simulations can rapidly estimate critical microstructure descriptors.
The estimated microstructure descriptors are predictive of Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness.
Targeting the most influential structural mediators preserves predictive accuracy while reducing computational expense.
The proposed method will predict Young's modulus within approximately ±10% of experiment.
The proposed method will predict yield strength within approximately ±10% of experiment.
The proposed method will predict toughness within approximately ±10% of experiment.
The proposed method will reduce computational demands by roughly an order of magnitude relative to traditional multiscale methods.
The method will lose reliability for compositions substantially outside its calibration space.
The method will lose reliability under high-temperature or non-tensile loading conditions when its VEC- and composition-based assumptions no longer hold.
Predictive accuracy and efficiency gains depend on the quality and representativeness of the high-fidelity training data.
